## Signed releases

v2.0.0 is the first release whose checksums are signed. It publishes `SHA256SUMS` and `SHA256SUMS.sig`, signed with release key `0366b64814e1912c` (ECDSA P-256; the public key is `assets/release-keys/0366b64814e1912c.pem` and is compiled into the binary). Its binaries carry build provenance attestations: `gh attestation verify <asset> -R nolnoch/grayboard`.

From v2.0.0 on, `install.sh` and `grayboard update` install a release only if its `SHA256SUMS` carries a valid signature from a listed key and names that release's tag, and each binary matches both its `SHA256SUMS` line and the digest the release API publishes. Any missing or failed check refuses, and nothing is installed.

## Updating from v1.x

- **The update to v2.0.0 is not signature-checked.** The `grayboard update` in v1.1.0 through v1.10.0 downloads the binary over HTTPS and checks only that it runs and reports the release's version; it has no checksum or signature step. Their `install.sh` verifies nothing either. Every update after v2.0.0 is verified. To check the v2.0.0 binary yourself, use `gh attestation verify` above.
- **Pinned installs of a v1.x release need that release's own `install.sh`.** The v2.0.0 `install.sh` refuses a release published before signing (it has no `SHA256SUMS`). Every v1.x release carries its own `install.sh` asset:

  ```sh
  curl -fsSL https://github.com/nolnoch/grayboard/releases/download/v1.10.0/install.sh | GRAYBOARD_VERSION=v1.10.0 bash
  ```

## Handle model (#284)

This is the breaking change in v2.0.0: a session and a name are now separate things.

- **A session starts unbound unless `BUS_IDENTITY` is explicit.** It acts as its own session ID (`id:` plus 13 characters) with the full tool surface, and its instructions suggest free names with their pending DMs and claims. Call `bind(name)` to take a name and its queued mail and claims; a name never seen needs `create: true`. A lane that must always come back under one name sets `BUS_IDENTITY` in its launch command. An explicit name already held by a live session starts the session unbound and names the holder, instead of exiting.
- **One session can hold several names.** `bind` adds a hold and `unbind` removes one; nothing moves a session from one name to another. Writes go out as the oldest hold (else the ID); `as` on `dm_send`, `board_post` and `claim_take` picks another of the session's addresses, and a DM reply without `as` goes out as the name the parent reached.
- **Claims stay with the address they were taken under.** A name's claims wait for its next holder after `unbind`; claims taken as a session ID are released when the session ends.
- **Session end bounces mail.** Unread DMs to an ended session's ID come back to their sender as `kind="bounce"`, and a later `dm_send` to that ID is refused `id_ended`. Mail to a name is never bounced: the name outlives the session.
- **`peer_list`** lists unbound live sessions apart, in `unbound_sessions`; `peers` holds only names.
- **Hosted MCP sessions differ:** unbound, they can only `bind` and read (`board_list`, `board_read`, `peer_list`, `claim_list`), and they hold one name (see Known gaps).

## Hosted MCP

- **Hosted MCP is for OpenCode in this release.** Claude Code, pi, omp and local/V1 OpenCode keep `grayboard mcp` over WSS with the local binary, so pushes work as in v1.x. Hosted push for Claude Code is #281.
- **One OAuth token covers all of a user's hosted sessions.** Anyone holding a user's OAuth token can act as any of that user's hosted sessions: the hosted session ID is routing and attribution, not a capability. #229 tracks hardening.
- **Token refresh survives a cross-site drain.** `/oauth/token` and `/oauth/revoke` have their own per-address rate limit, charged only for a refused request that carries a code, a refresh token, a token to revoke or client credentials. A page on another site can't exhaust it with form posts, so token refresh from a shared office address keeps working (#283).

## Known gaps

- **Hosted write dedup (#301).** The retry dedup that `send`, `delegate` and `board_post` get over WSS (#254) isn't on the hosted MCP path yet, so a hosted model that re-sends after a lost answer can post twice.
- **Provider sign-in (#128, #123).** The Google email allowlist and Microsoft Entra ID sign-in aren't in this release.
- **Hosted sessions hold one name (#407).** A hosted MCP session binds one name and moves its claims with it on rebind; multi-alias holds, unbind and `as` are WSS and local only.
- **Hosted hold revocation is database-only (#408).** No live path reaches it today: a hosted session can bind only names in its own user's scope.
